st.headline: Crypto shaken after Binance hack; Wilmar discloses sales to firms in haze probe: Markets this week
st.teaser: Temasek-backed Mapletree Investments is reported to be looking at an SGX IPO.
fullText: SINGAPORE – A multibillion-dollar hack at cryptocurrency exchange Binance shook the industry this week, sending prices lower amid concerns over the safety of investors’ assets on trading platforms.

Bitcoin fell about 5% over 24 hours since the Oct 29 incident, while Ether lost about 5.7%. Both extended their declines on Oct 30 before recovering some ground. On Nov 1, Bitcoin was trading at around US$77,450, while Ether was US$2,249.

About US$6.4 billion (S$8.2 billion) worth of cryptocurrencies was stolen on Binance within 30 minutes, with attackers linked to North Korea draining the platform’s internet-connected “hot wallets”, then rushing to exchange stolen stablecoins for cryptocurrencies such as Ether.
Unlike stablecoins, whose issuers can freeze assets, Bitcoin and Ether have no central issuer able to block their movement.
Approximately US$2.8 billion in stablecoins has been frozen by investigators, law enforcement agencies and stablecoin issuers so far.

In a video circulated on social media on Oct 30, Binance co-chief executive Richard Teng said the exchange has been working non-stop to recover the stolen assets, and added that it had reserved more than US$6.4 billion of its own money to cover all losses .
Teng said customer assets were safe and would not be used to cover the losses, and attributed Binance’s ability to absorb the losses to retained earnings and reinvestment into the business.
He added that withdrawals from the exchange, which have been suspended pending a security overhaul, are expected to resume by Nov 1 .
In Singapore, the Binance.com trading platform operates outside the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s (MAS) regulatory safeguards.

MAS placed the platform on its Investor Alert List in September 2021, warning that it was not regulated or licensed to provide payment services here. It also ordered Binance to stop providing such services in Singapore and cease soliciting business from residents.
Investors dealing with unregulated platforms forgo protections under MAS regulations.

Wilmar International on Oct 31 disclosed that it sold fertilisers and diesel for heavy equipment to six of the 10 companies named by the National Environment Agency (NEA) as linked to the haze caused by fires in Indonesia, generating revenue of around US$22.5 million in financial year 2025.

Updating its Oct 28 response to the regulatory arm of the Singapore Exchange (SGX RegCo) based on newly received information, Wilmar said none of the 10 companies named was its subsidiary. It added that it had no operational or supply-chain ties with six buyers and no operational, supply-chain or business relationship with the remaining four companies.
Shares of Wilmar took a beating during the week from rising raw material costs, which ate into its earnings, and elevated risks arising from a Government-led haze-related probe.
The shares fell 11% across the week to close Oct 30 at $3.01.

The conglomerate said its food products segment was hit by higher raw material costs, and the feed and industrial products segment by weaker soya bean crushing margins, triggering several analyst downgrades on the stock.

Wilmar said in a separate announcement that it has reviewed available information and assessed that the fires in Indonesia and transboundary haze have neither resulted in, nor are expected to result in, any material operational, financial, legal or regulatory impact on the company.
This was after 10 Singapore-registered, Indonesian oil palm-related companies, which included Wilmar, were issued preventive-measure notices by NEA under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act.
The Government has begun investigating companies linked to the haze, and on Oct 28 met the senior leadership of the Singapore businesses allegedly linked to haze-related activities.

Kuok Khoon Hong, chairman and CEO of Wilmar, was one of the executives present at the meeting. Besides Kuok, the bosses of Golden-Agri Resources, First Resources, Bumitama Agri, Indofood Agri Resources and Kencana Agri, and representatives from TSH Resources and the Sinar Mas Group, which includes Asia Pulp & Paper (APP), were also at the meeting.
On Oct 31, NEA said seven Singapore-registered companies had indicated their willingness to engage assessors to examine their links to fires contributing to transboundary haze.

Five companies – Wilmar, Golden Agri-Resources, APP Company, APP Company (China) and Indofood Agri Resources – have agreed to engage assessors from the Panel on Transboundary Haze and cooperate with the assessment process, following meetings with NEA.
The agency will also meet Kencana Agri, which has expressed willingness to voluntarily engage assessors.
NEA said it was awaiting written confirmation of First Resources’ participation in the assessment process.

In its statement, NEA also welcomed First Resources’ recent public statement that it was prepared to engage an investigation firm and a law firm to assess whether the group had any involvement in or connection with the fires that contributed to transboundary haze.
The Government on Oct 30 had appointed seven investigation and law firms and one individual to a specialist panel assembled to investigate companies linked to the transboundary haze.
US-listed tech stocks, including stalwarts like Alphabet, Amazon and Nvidia, had a rough week as fears around artificial intelligence spending collided with disappointing earnings.

Heavy infrastructure spending by mega-cap tech firms have led to cash flow strains and heightened investor sensitivity towards execution and investment returns, hitting the valuations of companies like Alphabet.
Google’s parent suffered its worst one-day percentage decline on record on Oct 29, falling as much as 12.6% and wiping out almost US$500 million in market value.
Investors dumped the stock after the company reported negative free cash flow of US$9.1 billion for the third quarter as a result of soaring AI-related costs. The stock closed on Oct 30 at US$278.22.

cna.headline: Heavy traffic expected at Singapore-Malaysia land checkpoints during Deepavali long weekend
cna.teaser: The Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) issued the travel advisory for Nov 6 to Nov 9, encouraging travellers to plan their journey ahead of time and consider travelling during non-peak hours.
fullText: SINGAPORE: Heavy traffic is expected at the Woodlands and Tuas checkpoints during the upcoming Deepavali long weekend.
The Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) on Sunday (Nov 1) issued the travel advisory for Nov 6 to Nov 9.
It encouraged travellers to plan their journey ahead of time and consider travelling during non-peak hours, such as early mornings and late evenings.
Travellers should check the traffic situation at the land checkpoints before starting their journey, ICA said.
ICA also strongly encouraged travellers to use QR codes generated via the MyICA mobile app for faster and more seamless immigration clearance.

It noted that initiatives such as QR code clearance and facial recognition for motorcyclists and pillion riders have increased clearance throughput by more than 35 per cent during departure peak periods - equivalent to an additional 7,600 travellers per hour compared with pre-COVID-19 levels in 2019.
Since Sep 30, short-term visitors entering Singapore through the land checkpoints who submit their SG Arrival Card via the MyICA app must update the app to the latest version before doing so.

Travellers entering Singapore by foreign-registered car must also ensure that the vehicle has a valid Vehicle Entry Permit (VEP) before submitting their SG Arrival Card. They will not be able to complete the submission without a valid VEP.
"While driving on roads leading to and within the land checkpoints, motorists are to cooperate with ICA officers, observe lane discipline and comply with traffic rules," said ICA.
"Queue cutting disrupts traffic flow and delays other travellers. Those caught queue cutting will be directed to make a U-turn and re-join the queue from the back."
ICA added that it will take firm action against travellers who do not comply with its officers' instructions or who commit traffic offences at the checkpoints.
During the recent September school holidays from Sep 4 to Sep 14, more than 6.1 million travellers crossed both land checkpoints, with the volume peaking at more than 599,000 on Sep 4.

This set a new record, ICA said, surpassing the previous peak of more than 598,000 crossings on Jun 19, 2026. Car travellers departing during peak hours experienced waiting times of up to three hours for immigration clearance, due to traffic tailbacks from Malaysia.
During that travel period, 27 motorists were caught for traffic-related offences and dangerous road behaviour.

listening.title: Singapore Expands Electric Bus Fleet in Public Transport Push
listening.transcript: Singapore's Land Transport Authority has unveiled plans to rollout hundreds of new electric buses across major public routes by next year. The initiative aims to significantly reduce carbon emissions from city transit while enhancing commuter comfort. Officials noted that charging infrastructure is being upgraded rapidly to support the expanding green fleet across island-wide depots.

economistArticle.title: The Poisoned Chalice at Frankfurt
paras: When Christine Lagarde assumed leadership of the European Central Bank, the eurozone was grappling with sluggish growth and stubbornly low inflation. Years later, as whispers of her departure grow louder across European capitals, the financial landscape appears even more precarious. Her successor will step into an institution caught between sticky core inflation, persistent industrial stagnation in Germany, and deepening geopolitical fragmentation.

The challenges facing Frankfurt are compounded by political volatility across key member states. Fiscal policy remains fractured across the bloc, leaving monetary policy to bear an unfair share of the economic burden. Central bankers must attempt to maintain price stability without triggering a severe credit contraction in already fragile national economies.

Furthermore, the ECB's task is complicated by widening interest rate divergence across global markets. As foreign central banks navigate their own domestic priorities, European monetary authorities risk currency depreciation if they loosen policy settings too aggressively. Navigating this delicate balance will require exceptional diplomatic finesse alongside analytical rigor.

Whoever inherits the top job at the ECB will quickly discover that quiet institutional consensus is a luxury of the past. Balancing the divergent demands of hawkish northern member states and heavily indebted southern economies will make the role an unenviable task in a deeply troubled economic era.
economistArticle.cn:
当克里斯蒂娜·拉加德出任欧洲中央银行行长时，欧元区正面临经济增长缓慢和通胀持续低迷的困境。多年后的今天，随着有关她即将离任的传言在欧洲各国首都流传，金融局势显得更加摇摇欲坠。她的继任者将接手一个夹在粘性核心通胀、德国持续工业停滞以及日益加剧的地缘政治碎片化之间的机构。

法兰克福面临的挑战因主要成员国的政治波动而变得更加复杂。整个区的财政政策依然撕裂，使得货币政策承担了不公平的经济重担。中央银行家们必须努力维持物价稳定，同时避免在本已脆弱的国家经济中引发严重的信贷紧缩。

此外，全球市场日益扩大加剧的利率分歧使欧洲央行的任务更加复杂。随着外国中央银行应对各自国内的优先事项，如果欧洲货币当局过于激进地放松政策设定，将面临本币贬值的风险。要保持这种微妙的平衡，不仅需要精湛的技术严谨性，还需要卓越的外交技巧。

无论谁接任欧洲央行的最高职位，都会很快发现，安静的机构共识已成为过去的奢望。平衡北部鹰派成员国与负债累累的南部经济体之间的分歧需求，将使这一职位成为深陷困境的经济时代中一项令人望而生畏的任务。

gems.s: Fiscal policy remains fractured across the bloc, leaving monetary policy to bear an unfair share of the economic burden.
gems.why: This sentence uses a clear cause-and-effect structure ending with a participial clause ('leaving monetary policy to...'), neatly illustrating how to express complex macroeconomic tensions concisely. 句子结尾使用分词短语结构引出后果，简洁精炼地展示了如何表达复杂的宏观经济矛盾。

gems.s: Balancing the divergent demands of hawkish northern member states and heavily indebted southern economies will make the role an unenviable task in a deeply troubled economic era.
gems.why: The author uses contrasting paired modifiers ('hawkish northern' versus 'heavily indebted southern') to vividly summarize internal geopolitical divides in policy creation. 作者通过两组鲜明对比的修饰词，生动勾勒出政策制定中内部地缘经济的分歧。
